title: Bank teller queue simulation
instructions:
Implement two interacting modules, `customers.py` and `bank.py`.
`customers.py` exports a frozen dataclass `Customer(customer_id: str, arrival: int, duration: int)`
with these three fields, and `parse_customers(text: str) -> list[Customer]`:
- Each nonblank line is exactly `id,arrival,duration`. Strip whitespace around fields. IDs must be
  nonempty and unique within the input. Arrival and duration must consist only of ASCII digits;
  leading zeros are allowed. Arrival is nonnegative and duration is positive. Malformed lines,
  duplicate IDs, or invalid numbers raise `ValueError`. Blank lines are ignored; preserve input order.
  No quoting or comments are supported. Directly constructed Customers are assumed valid.
`bank.py` imports the customer module and exports:
- `simulate(customers: list[Customer], tellers: int) -> list[dict]`. Nonpositive tellers raises
  `ValueError`, including for an empty customer list. Otherwise process customers by increasing
  arrival, retaining input order for ties (a single FIFO queue). Tellers are numbered 0 to tellers-1.
  Each customer starts as soon as a teller can serve them. Among tellers available at that start
  time, choose the lowest teller number. Service cannot be interrupted. A teller is free exactly
  at the end of its previous service. Return records in queue order with exactly these keys:
  `customer_id`, `teller`, `arrival`, `start`, `end`, `wait`; times are integer units,
  end = start + duration and wait = start - arrival. Do not reorder or mutate the input list.
- `summarize(records: list[dict], tellers: int) -> dict`. Accept the records from simulate;
  reject nonpositive tellers with `ValueError`. Return exactly `{"served": int, "total_wait": int,
  "max_wait": int, "last_end": int, "busy": list[int]}`. Busy has one entry per teller, summing
  service durations; unused tellers have zero. On empty records the three time metrics are zero.
No real time, sleeping, randomness, or I/O is involved.

## Files
- `customers.py`
- `bank.py`
